Long-term firm contracts for the sale of electric energy to private utilities (for resale) by TVA are complicated by a provision of the Tennessee Valley Authority Act of 1933 2/ which provides for the cancellation of all contracts "made with private companies or individuals for the sale of power, which power is to be resold for profit -- upon five years notice in writing if the board needs such power to supply the demands of States, counties or municipalities." These considerations, plus the long lead times required for construction of large generating plants, eliminate the purchase of power from the TVA as a practical alternative to Bad Creek.
The purchase of power is not an equivalent alternative to the proposed project for another important reason: it would not provide Applicant's system with a means of storing the elctric energy which can be generated by large base-load nuclear and efficient fossil-fueled steam plants during offpeak hours. This excess energy can be returned to Applicant's system load during peak-load hours with substantial savings in production costs and fossil fuels. This characteristic of the pumped storage project is unique among the alternative types of generation and power supply commercially available for large scale operation.
8.2.9 Denial of Application for License
If the application for license to construct the Bad Creek Pumped Storage Project is denied, then either the Applicant's electrical generating system would be operating with less than desired reliability or one of the alternative power sources previously discussed would have to be constructed with its resultant environmental impacts. The Bad Creek Project, with the possible exception of the Long Spur Ridge alternative, is the lowest cost power source available to the Applicant, commensurate with its system needs. Therefore, construction of an alternative power source would add more overall costs to the Applicant's rate base, thereby burdening the consumer with higher prices.
The heavy scheduling of nuclear generation by the Applicant favors construction of an energy storage power plant such as Bad Creek. Without Bad Creek, the nuclear stations would frequently have to operate at reduced load
